newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Regent's resolutions on Pioneer defeated.
newsitem.headline: Regent's resolutions on Pioneer defeated.

text.p: Resolutions by Regent Fund Management Ltd to shake up Pioneer Industries International (Holdings) Ltd were defeated in a general meeting on Tuesday.
Shareholders representing 185 million shares voted against the resolutions and 89 million shares voted for them, Pioneer deputy managing director Kenneth Gaw said.
Pioneer has an issued share capital of 305.95 million shares as at March 31, 1996.

Regent, which holds 20 percent of Pioneer, proposed resolutions to call for appointment of 13 additional directors to Pioneer's board, and for a reduction to the discount of market value of shares they held in the company.
Regent had said Pioneer share prices were trading at over 50-percent discount to its true net asset value, and drastic steps must be taken to improve share performance.
They could include selling its prime asset, a 3.77 percent stake in Bangkok Bank Ltd, Thailand's biggest bank.
Regent estimates Pioneer's net asset value at HK$12.46 per share after tax. Pioneer shares closed at HK$6.10 on Tuesday, valuing the company at HK$1.87 billion.

Regent also claimed Pioneer's stake in Bangkok Bank was actually bigger than the company admitted due to another 6.5 million foreign shares held through a 49-percent stake in a Liberian company Central Asia Ltd, which increases Pioneer's stake in Bangkok Bank to 4.4 percent.

"It (Regent's resolutions being defeated) is expected as Gaw family holds the controlling stake in the company," said James Mellon after the general meeting, adding the fund aimed to protect the interests of shareholders.
The Gaw family held 26.33 of the company as at the end of December 1995.
Mellon said Regent also queried the academic qualification of Pioneer chairman Anthony Gaw.
Regent Fund will continue holding the shares despite having its resolutions defeated, Mellon added.
